programme: No single module ties these twelve together. They split into at least three unrelated clusters: (1) a MYC/E2F cell-cycle cluster - TFDP1 (partnering E2F on RB1/CDK2/CDK4/MYC/PCNA/CCNE1/CCNA2), MXD1 (a MYC antagonist via MAX on the same TERT/CCND2/ODC1 axis), and MAZ (a MYC-associated zinc finger on overlapping MMP/VEGFA targets); (2) an NF-kB/innate-inflammatory cluster - NFKBIB (IkBbeta gating IL1B/PTGS2/TNF/CXCL8/CCL5), CEBPG (the same acute-phase genes plus S100A8/CSF3/NOS2), and ETV5 (IL17A/IL17F/IL21/IL10, a Th17-cytokine target set); and (3) lineage-restricted developmental factors with no stated role in gut or skin biology - PAX8 (thyroid genes TG/TPO/SLC5A5/TSHB), TCF3/E2A (B-lymphopoiesis genes CD79A/CD79B/VPREB1/PAX5/EBF1), NPAS1 (EPO/TH/ARNT), NACC1 (a 4-gene stemness/quiescence set), and MSC/musculin (Treg genes FOXP3/CTLA4/IL2RA/IL10, whose retrieved papers are actually about 'mesenchymal stem cell' therapy, an unrelated homonym, not the musculin transcription factor). No shared complex, cofactor, or single pathway node connects these three clusters.
role_in_a: Fragmented across clusters with no unifying role: PPARA has an independent IBS expression signal (metabolic/anti-inflammatory), but the cell-cycle cluster (TFDP1/MXD1/MAZ) has no documented proliferative phenotype in IBS mucosa, and the inflammatory cluster (CEBPG/NFKBIB/ETV5) has no established Th17/NF-kB signature specific to IBS.
role_in_b: Equally fragmented: the cell-cycle cluster would fit psoriasis's hallmark keratinocyte hyperproliferation, and ETV5's IL17A/IL17F/IL21 targets sit inside psoriasis's well-established IL-17 axis, but neither PPARA, PAX8, NPAS1, NACC1, nor TCF3 has a documented psoriasis role in this record, so no single programme spans the disease.
shared_axis: There is no candidate axis that covers both diseases without contradiction: the cell-cycle cluster maps onto psoriasis's proliferative keratinocyte biology but IBS is not a hyperproliferative mucosal disease, and the NF-kB/Th17-leaning cluster maps onto psoriasis's IL-17 axis but IBS lacks an established inflammatory signature of that kind. Concordance across patient groups here looks like independent network-inference agreement, not a shared mechanism.
reasoning: The four highest-confidence factors alone (TCF3 27/32, CEBPG 25/32, NACC1 24/32, PPARA 22/32) span four mutually unrelated programmes (B-lymphopoiesis, myeloid inflammation, stemness/quiescence, lipid metabolism), which is the opposite of what a real shared module should look like. Retrieved literature places almost nothing: only PPARA has a direct IBS expression citation, and the apparent MSC evidence is a gene-symbol collision with 'mesenchymal stem cell' therapy papers, not the musculin transcription factor, so it should not count as support.
support: 31833409 - reports PPARA expression differences in IBS patients, the only clean factor-disease placement in the set; 41480397, 41571652, 41007656, 36925706 - concern mesenchymal stem cell (cell-therapy) interventions in IBS-D and psoriasis respectively, not the MSC/musculin transcription factor, so despite naming 'MSC' they do not evidence this factor; 35620404, 23977377 - address colitis/UC rather than IBS; 41699832 - psoriasis paper where PPARA's involvement is unclear from the excerpt; 38455905 - mentions IBS only in a stress/epigenetics context, not PAX8 specifically; remaining factors (CEBPG, NACC1, TFDP1, MAZ, ETV5, NPAS1, MXD1, NFKBIB) - none found.
how_to_falsify: Take matched IBS colorectal mucosa and psoriatic skin biopsies and test whether the proposed cell-cycle trio (TFDP1, MXD1, MAZ) or the inflammatory trio (CEBPG, NFKBIB, ETV5) actually co-occupy the same regulatory elements (ChIP-seq or CUT&RUN for co-binding, or reporter assays at shared target promoters like PTGS2/IL1B) in both tissues, and whether that co-binding tracks with disease activity. Finding tissue-specific, non-overlapping binding for each cluster - or no cell-cycle re-entry signature in IBS mucosa - would confirm that the network-level concordance reflects independent, tissue-specific regulation rather than a shared module.
caveats: Tissue pairing is colorectal (IBS) vs skin (psoriasis), an anatomically and embryologically distant comparison; support is drawn from 32 patient-group comparisons across only 2 independent cohort pairs, so 'concordance' reflects agreement of network inference across sub-cohorts of the same two underlying studies rather than broad replication. Only NRF1 and DNMT3L were excluded as single-view (no tissue-generic exclusion list was supplied for this pair, so that filter cannot be checked here). The MSC gene-symbol collision with 'mesenchymal stem cell' in the literature is a specific trap in this record and should not be treated as evidence for the musculin transcription factor.
